newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/8 to 1/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/8 to 1/4.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended Friday's abbreviated session down 1/8 to 1/4 point in sympathy with U.S. Treasury bond weakness.
"It's really a holiday day," one trader said. "Everybody's trying to get out of town."
The Public Securities Association recommended a 1400 EST close for municipals Friday, and a full close Monday to observe Veteran's Day.
While the broader muni market ended down 1/8 to 1/4 point, dollar bonds ended down 1/8 point, a municipal analyst said. High-grade issues worsened by two basis points, he said. Activity was light.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 10/32 at 99-29/32 to yield 6.51 percent. Following Thursday's rally, prices opened lower Friday as players took profits, but losses deeped after large funds and money managers appeared square accounts ahead of the long weekend.

In addition, the Commerce Department reported that wholesale inventories dropped 1.3 percent in September against a 0.1 percent fall the previous month. The decline was the biggest since February 1982. One economist observed that the market probably thinks less inventory accumulation in the third quarter may mean a stronger rebound in the fourth
Back in muni cash, a few bid lists circulated, market sources said.
"We've got some intermediate bond fund and money managers selling their pre-res and some 10-year stuff," a trader said. "The long end, we really haven't seen a lot of sellers."
Another market participant said AMG Data Services figures for the latest reporting week showed $323 million of fresh cash flowed into municipal bond funds.

Turning to next week's primary market, volume is expected to be light. Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are seen totaling $2.268 billion in 105 offerings for the week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales are expected to total $808 million in 66 offerings, with the largest a $184 million Virginia Transportation Board on Thursday.
Negotiated sales total $1.46 billion in 39 offerings. The largest issue is a $180 million Chicago Toll Bridge deal through PaineWebber Inc.
